## 9. AI TELLS (Forbidden Patterns)

Avoid these signatures unless the brief explicitly asks for them.

### 9.A Visual & CSS
* **NO neon / outer glows** by default. Use inner borders or subtle tinted shadows.
* **NO pure black (`#000000`).** Off-black, zinc-950, or charcoal.
* **NO oversaturated accents.** Desaturate to blend with neutrals.
* **NO excessive gradient text** for large headers.
* **NO custom mouse cursors.** Outdated, accessibility-hostile, perf-hostile.

### 9.B Typography
* **AVOID Inter as default.** See Section 4.1. Override path exists.
* **NO oversized H1s** that just scream. Control hierarchy with weight + color, not raw scale.
* **Serif constraints:** Serif for editorial / luxury / publication. Not for dashboards.

### 9.C Layout & Spacing
* **Mathematically perfect** padding and margins. No floating elements with awkward gaps.
* **NO 3-column equal feature cards.** The generic "three identical cards horizontally" feature row is banned. Use 2-column zig-zag, asymmetric grid, scroll-pinned, or horizontal-scroll alternative.

### 9.D Content & Data ("Jane Doe" Effect)
* **NO generic names.** "John Doe", "Sarah Chan", "Jack Su" → use creative, realistic, locale-appropriate names.
* **NO generic avatars.** No SVG "egg" or Lucide user icons → use believable photo placeholders or specific styling.
* **NO fake-perfect numbers.** Avoid `99.99%`, `50%`, `1234567`. Use organic, messy data (`47.2%`, `+1 (312) 847-1928`).
* **NO startup-slop brand names.** "Acme", "Nexus", "SmartFlow", "Cloudly" → invent contextual, premium names that sound real.
* **NO filler verbs.** "Elevate", "Seamless", "Unleash", "Next-Gen", "Revolutionize" → concrete verbs only.

### 9.E External Resources & Components
* **NO hand-rolled SVG icons.** Use Phosphor / HugeIcons / Radix / Tabler. Lucide on explicit request only.
* **Hand-rolled decorative SVGs strongly discouraged** as default (see Section 4.8).
* **NO div-based fake screenshots.** Never build a fake product UI out of `<div>` rectangles to simulate a screenshot. Use real images, generated images, or skip the preview.
* **NO broken Unsplash links.** Use `https://picsum.photos/seed/{descriptive-string}/{w}/{h}`, or generated photo placeholders, or actual assets.
* **shadcn/ui customization:** Allowed, but NEVER in default state. Customize radii, colors, shadows, typography to the project aesthetic.
* **Production-Ready Cleanliness:** Code visually clean, memorable, meticulously refined.

### 9.F Production-Test Tells (banned outright)

These patterns came out of real LLM-generated landing-page tests. They are the signatures the model defaults to when it tries to "look designed." Treat them as hard bans unless the brief explicitly calls for one.

**Hero & top-of-page**
* **NO version labels in the hero.** `V0.6`, `v2.0`, `BETA`, `INVITE-ONLY PREVIEW`, `EARLY ACCESS`, `ALPHA` - banned as default eyebrows. Only acceptable when the brief is explicitly about a product launch / preview status.
* **NO "Brand · No. 01"-style sub-eyebrows.** "Marrow · No. 01 · The 6-quart" type micro-meta lines. Skip them.

**Section numbering & micro-labels**
* **NO section-number eyebrows.** `00 / INDEX`, `001 · Capabilities`, `002 · Featured commission`, `06 · how it works`, `05 · The honest table` - banned. Eyebrows should name the topic in plain language, not enumerate.
* **NO `01 / 4`-style pagination on images or bento tiles.** If the user can count, they don't need the label.
* **NO `Scroll · 001 Capabilities`-style scroll cues.** A simple arrow or "Scroll" is enough; no section-number prefix.
* **NO "Index of Work, 2018 - 2026"-style range labels** as eyebrows. Just say what the section is.

**Separators & dots**
* **The middle-dot (`·`) is rationed.** Maximum 1 per line in metadata strips. Do NOT use it as the default separator for everything ("foo · bar · baz · qux · quux"). If you need a separator family, prefer line breaks, hairlines, or columns.
* **NO decorative colored status dots on every list/nav/badge.** A colored dot before "ONE Q4 SLOT OPEN" or before every nav link, or every task row - banned by default. Acceptable only when the dot conveys actual semantic state (a server status, an availability flag) and is used sparingly.

**Em-dashes & typography flourishes**
* **NO em-dash (`—`) as a design element OR anywhere else.** See Section 9.G below for the complete, non-negotiable ban. The em-dash character is forbidden in headlines, eyebrows, pills, body copy, quotes, attribution, captions, button text, and alt text. Use the regular hyphen (`-`).
* **NO `<br>`-broken-and-italicized headlines** as a default "design move." "for thirty\<br\>*years.*" type splits. Headlines should read naturally first, get clever only when the brief demands it.
* **NO vertical rotated text** ("INDEX OF WORK, 2018 - 2026" rotated 90°). Agency-portfolio cliché. Use it only when the brief is explicitly agency / Awwwards / experimental AND it serves a real composition purpose.
* **NO crosshair / hairline grid lines as decoration.** Vertical and horizontal lines drawn just to make the page "feel designed" - banned. Use them only when they organize real content.

**Fake product previews**
* **NO div-based fake product UI in the hero** (fake task list, fake terminal, fake dashboard built from styled divs). It is the #1 LLM-design Tell. Use a real screenshot, a generated image, a real component preview, or none at all.
* **NO fake version footers** ("v0.6.2-rc.1", "last sync 4s ago · main") inside fake screenshots. Adds nothing, screams AI.

**Marketing-copy Tells**
* **NO "Quietly in use at" / "Quietly trusted by"** social-proof headers. Use natural language: "Trusted by", "Used at", "Customers include", or skip the heading entirely if the logos speak.
* **NO "From the field" / "Field notes" / "Currently on the bench" / "On our desks" / "Loose plates" style poetic labels** on quote, blog, or sidebar sections. Reads as performative-craftsman. Use plain functional labels ("Testimonials", "Latest writing", "Now working on") or skip the label.
* **NO "We respect the French ones"-style** mock-humble industry-references in body copy. Cute and AI-y.
* **NO weather / locale strips** ("LIS 14:23 · 18°C") in headers/footers unless the brief is explicitly about a place / time-zone-distributed studio.
* **NO micro-meta-sentences under eyebrows.** Sentences like *"Each of these is a feature we ship today, not a roadmap promise. The list will stay short on purpose."* sitting under a section heading are clutter. Eyebrow + Headline + Body is enough.
* **NO generic step labels.** "Stage 1 / Stage 2 / Stage 3", "Step 1 / Step 2 / Step 3", "Phase 01 / Phase 02 / Phase 03", "Pass One / Pass Two / Pass Three". Banned. The actual step content is the label. If you must show progression, use the verb-noun directly ("Install", "Configure", "Ship") not "Stage 1: Install".

**Pills, labels and version stamps**
* **NO pills/labels/tags overlaid on images.** No `<span>` overlays on photos with tags like `Brand · 02`, `PLATE · BRAND`, `Field notes - journal`. Either let the image speak alone, or add a caption directly below (outside the image).
* **NO photo-credit captions as decoration.** Strings like `Field study no. 12 · Ines Caetano`, `Plate 03 · House archive`, `Frame XII · 35mm` under stock/picsum images are pretentious. Photo credit is allowed ONLY when there is a real photographer being credited for a real photo (with permission). Otherwise: skip the caption or use a one-line functional caption ("The 6-quart, in Sage.").
* **NO version footers on marketing pages.** Footer strings like `v1.4.2`, `Build 0048`, `last sync 4s ago · main` are CLI / devtool fixtures, not landing-page content. Banned on marketing/landing/portfolio pages.
* **NO "Reservation 412 of 800"-style live-stock counters** as decoration. Only if the brief is explicitly a limited-run waitlist with real data.

**Decoration text strips**
* **NO decoration text strip at hero bottom.** Patterns like `BRAND. MOTION. SPATIAL.`, `TYPE / FORM / MOTION`, `DESIGN · BUILD · SHIP`, `ESTD. 2018 · LISBON · BRAND. MOTION. SPATIAL.` as a small mono-caps strip across the bottom of the hero are an agency-portfolio cliché. Banned by default. Only acceptable when the strip carries real, navigable links (sticky bottom nav) or real status info (cookie banner, build info on a docs site).
* **NO floating top-right sub-text in section headings.** Pattern: section has a giant left-aligned headline; in the top-right corner of the same section header there is a small explainer paragraph floating with no clear alignment to anything else. That floater is the Tell. Either put the sub-text directly under the headline, or build a clean 2-column header (left: headline, right: aligned body), but not a tiny corner paragraph.

**Lists, dividers and scoring**
* **NO `border-t` + `border-b` on every row of a long list / spec table.** Pick one (bottom-border between rows OR top-border above the group) and use it sparsely. A 10-row spec table with hairlines under each row is the laziest layout - see Section 4.9 for alternative UI components.
* **NO scoring/progress bars with filled background tracks** as comparison visuals. If you need to show "X out of Y" comparisons, prefer a number + small icon, or a tiny inline bar WITHOUT a background track. Big filled `bg-zinc-200` tracks with a partial fill on top are dashboard-UI clutter on a landing page.

**Locale, time, scroll cues**
* **Locale / city-name / time / weather strips are banned for 99% of briefs.** "Lisbon, working with founders" in the hero, "1200-690 Lisbon, Portugal" in the footer, "Lisbon 14:23 · 18°C" in the nav. These are agency-portfolio decoration tells. Allowed ONLY when: the brief explicitly describes a globally-distributed studio with timezone-relevant work, OR a travel-focused brand, OR a real-world physical venue. A single contact-address mention in the footer is fine; an atmospheric locale strip is not.
* **Scroll cues are banned.** `Scroll`, `↓ scroll`, `Scroll to explore`, `Scroll to walk through it`, animated mouse-wheel icons. If the user has not scrolled yet, they are looking at the hero. They know what scroll is. The bottom of the viewport does not need a label.
* **ZERO decorative status dots by default.** A coloured dot before nav items, before list rows, before badges, before status labels is a Tell. Only acceptable when conveying real semantic state (a live indicator on actual server status, a live availability flag) and limited to one per page section.

### 9.G EM-DASH BAN (the single most-violated Tell)

**Em-dash (`—`) is COMPLETELY banned.** It is the LLM's signature stylistic crutch and it is the #1 visual Tell in production tests. There is no "limited use" allowance, no "natural language frequency" allowance, no "in body copy is fine" allowance. None.

* **Banned in headlines.** Use a period or a comma.
* **Banned in eyebrows / labels / pills / button text / image captions / nav items.** Replace with line breaks, columns, or hairlines.
* **Banned in body copy.** Restructure the sentence: two sentences with a period, OR a comma, OR parentheses, OR a colon.
* **Banned in quote attribution.** Use a normal hyphen with spaces (` - `) or a line break + smaller-weight name.
* **Banned in en-dash form too (`–`) when used as a separator.** Date ranges (`2018-2026`) use a hyphen. Number ranges (`€40-80k`) use a hyphen.

The ONLY permitted dash characters on the page are:
* Regular hyphen `-` (for compound words, ranges, line dividers in markup)
* Minus sign in math (`-5°C`)

If your output contains a single `—` or `–` anywhere visible to the user, the output fails the Pre-Flight Check and must be rewritten.

This rule is non-negotiable. The agent has historically ignored em-dash limits when phrased as "use sparingly." The phrasing here is binary: zero em-dashes.

## 10. REFERENCE VOCABULARY (Pattern Names the Agent Should Know)

This is a vocabulary, not a library. The agent should KNOW these pattern names to communicate about them, design with them in mind, and reach for them when the design read calls for them. **Implementations and code sketches live in the Block Library (Section 12), which is populated iteratively.**

### Hero Paradigms
* **Asymmetric Split Hero** - Text on one side, asset on the other, generous white space.
* **Editorial Manifesto Hero** - Large type, no asset, almost-poster.
* **Video / Media Mask Hero** - Type cut out as mask over video background.
* **Kinetic-Type Hero** - Animated typography as the primary visual.
* **Curtain-Reveal Hero** - Hero parts on scroll like a curtain.
* **Scroll-Pinned Hero** - Hero stays pinned while content scrolls behind.

### Navigation & Menus
* **Mac OS Dock Magnification** - Edge nav, icons scale fluidly on hover.
* **Magnetic Button** - Pulls toward cursor.
* **Gooey Menu** - Sub-items detach like viscous liquid.
* **Dynamic Island** - Morphing pill for status / alerts.
* **Contextual Radial Menu** - Circular menu expanding at click point.
* **Floating Speed Dial** - FAB springing into curved secondary actions.
* **Mega Menu Reveal** - Full-screen dropdown, stagger-fade content.

### Layout & Grids
* **Bento Grid** - Asymmetric tile grouping (Apple Control Center).
* **Masonry Layout** - Staggered grid, no fixed row height.
* **Chroma Grid** - Borders / tiles with subtle animating gradients.
* **Split-Screen Scroll** - Two halves sliding in opposite directions.
* **Sticky-Stack Sections** - Sections that pin and stack on scroll.

### Cards & Containers
* **Parallax Tilt Card** - 3D tilt tracking mouse coordinates.
* **Spotlight Border Card** - Borders illuminate under cursor.
* **Glassmorphism Panel** - Frosted glass with inner refraction.
* **Holographic Foil Card** - Iridescent rainbow shift on hover.
* **Tinder Swipe Stack** - Physical card stack, swipe-away.
* **Morphing Modal** - Button expands into its own dialog.

### Scroll Animations
* **Sticky Scroll Stack** - Cards stick and physically stack.
* **Horizontal Scroll Hijack** - Vertical scroll → horizontal pan.
* **Locomotive / Sequence Scroll** - Video / 3D sequence tied to scrollbar.
* **Zoom Parallax** - Central background image zooming on scroll.
* **Scroll Progress Path** - SVG line drawing along scroll.
* **Liquid Swipe Transition** - Page transition like viscous liquid.

### Galleries & Media
* **Dome Gallery** - 3D panoramic gallery.
* **Coverflow Carousel** - 3D carousel with angled edges.
* **Drag-to-Pan Grid** - Boundless draggable canvas.
* **Accordion Image Slider** - Narrow strips expanding on hover.
* **Hover Image Trail** - Mouse leaves popping image trail.
* **Glitch Effect Image** - RGB-channel shift on hover.

### Typography & Text
* **Kinetic Marquee** - Endless text bands reversing on scroll.
* **Text Mask Reveal** - Massive type as transparent window to video.
* **Text Scramble Effect** - Matrix-style decoding on load / hover.
* **Circular Text Path** - Text curving along spinning circle.
* **Gradient Stroke Animation** - Outlined text with running gradient.
* **Kinetic Typography Grid** - Letters dodging the cursor.

### Micro-Interactions & Effects
* **Particle Explosion Button** - CTA shatters into particles on success.
* **Liquid Pull-to-Refresh** - Reload indicator like detaching droplets.
* **Skeleton Shimmer** - Shifting light reflection across placeholders.
* **Directional Hover-Aware Button** - Fill enters from cursor's exact side.
* **Ripple Click Effect** - Wave from click coordinates.
* **Animated SVG Line Drawing** - Vectors drawing themselves in real time.
* **Mesh Gradient Background** - Organic lava-lamp blobs.
* **Lens Blur Depth** - Background UI blurred to focus foreground action.

### Animation Library Choice
* **Motion (`motion/react`)** - default for UI / Bento / state-change motion.
* **GSAP + ScrollTrigger** - for full-page scrolltelling and scroll hijacks. Isolate in dedicated leaf components with `useEffect` cleanup.
* **Three.js / WebGL** - for canvas backgrounds and 3D scenes. Same isolation rule.
* **NEVER mix GSAP / Three.js with Motion in the same component tree.** They fight over the same frames.

## 11. REDESIGN PROTOCOL

This skill handles **greenfield builds AND redesigns**. Misclassifying the mode is the single biggest source of bad redesign output.

### 11.A Detect the Mode (first action)
* **Greenfield** - no existing site, or full overhaul approved. Dial baseline from Section 1.
* **Redesign - Preserve** - modernise without breaking the brand. Audit first, extract brand tokens, evolve gradually.
* **Redesign - Overhaul** - new visual language on top of existing content. Treat as greenfield for visuals; preserve content and IA.

If ambiguous, ask **once**: *"Should this redesign preserve the existing brand, or are we starting visually from scratch?"*

### 11.B Audit Before Touching
Document the current state before proposing changes:
* **Brand tokens** - primary / accent colors, type stack, logo treatment, radii.
* **Information architecture** - page tree, primary nav, key conversion paths.
* **Content blocks** - what exists, what's doing work, what's filler.
* **Patterns to preserve** - signature interactions, recognisable hero, copy voice.
* **Patterns to retire** - AI-slop tells, broken layouts, dead links, generic stock imagery, perf traps.
* **Dial reading of the existing site** - infer current `DESIGN_VARIANCE` / `MOTION_INTENSITY` / `VISUAL_DENSITY`. That's your starting point, not the baseline.
* **SEO baseline** - current ranking pages, meta titles, structured data, OG cards. **SEO migration is the #1 redesign risk.**

### 11.C Preservation Rules
* **Do not change information architecture** unless asked. Keep page slugs, anchor IDs, primary nav labels stable for SEO and muscle memory.
* **Extract brand colors before applying Section 4.2.** A brand that is already purple stays purple - apply the LILA RULE's override.
* **Preserve copy voice** unless asked for a rewrite. Visual modernisation ≠ content rewrite.
* **Honor existing accessibility wins.** Do not regress focus states, alt text, keyboard nav, contrast.
* **Respect existing analytics events.** Do not rename buttons, form fields, section IDs that downstream tracking depends on.

### 11.D Modernisation Levers (priority order)
Apply in order - stop when the brief is satisfied:
1. **Typography refresh** - biggest visual lift per unit of risk.
2. **Spacing & rhythm** - increase section padding, fix vertical rhythm.
3. **Color recalibration** - desaturate, unify neutrals, keep brand accent.
4. **Motion layer** - add `MOTION_INTENSITY`-appropriate micro-interactions to existing components.
5. **Hero & key-section recomposition** - restructure top-of-funnel using Section 10 vocabulary.
6. **Full block replacement** - only when the existing block is unsalvageable.

### 11.E Decision Tree: Targeted Evolution vs Full Redesign
* IA, content, and SEO sound → **targeted evolution** (Levers 1-4). ~70% of value at ~40% of risk.
* Visual debt is structural (broken IA, no design system, broken mobile) → **full redesign** with strict content preservation.
* Brand itself is changing → **greenfield**.

### 11.F What Never Changes Silently
Never modify without explicit user approval:
* URL structure / route slugs.
* Primary nav labels.
* Form field names or order (breaks analytics + autofill).
* Brand logo or wordmark.
* Existing legal / consent / cookie copy.

## 13. OUT OF SCOPE

This skill is NOT for:
* Dashboards / dense product UI / admin panels (use Fluent, Carbon, Atlassian, or Polaris from Section 2.A).
* Data tables (use TanStack Table or AG Grid).
* Multi-step forms / wizards (use Form-specific patterns; this skill won't make them better).
* Code editors (use Monaco / CodeMirror with their official skinning).
* Native mobile (use Apple HIG / Material directly).
* Realtime collab UIs (presence, cursors, OT-aware - different problem class).

If the brief is one of the above, **say so explicitly**, point to the right tool, and only apply this skill's marketing-page / about-page / landing-page parts to the surfaces where they apply.

## 14. FINAL PRE-FLIGHT CHECK

Run this matrix before outputting code. This is the last filter.

**THIS IS NOT OPTIONAL. Run every box. If any box fails, the output is not done.**

- [ ] **Brief inference** declared (Section 0.B one-liner)?
- [ ] **Dial values** explicit and reasoned from the brief, not silently using baseline?
- [ ] **Design system** chosen from Section 2 if applicable, or aesthetic labeled honestly?
- [ ] **Redesign mode** detected and audit performed (if applicable, Section 11)?
- [ ] **ZERO em-dashes (`—`) anywhere on the page.** Headlines, eyebrows, pills, body, quotes, attribution, captions, buttons, alt text. Zero. (Section 9.G - non-negotiable.)
- [ ] **Page Theme Lock**: ONE theme (light, dark, or auto) for the whole page. No section flips to inverted mode mid-page (Section 4.11)?
- [ ] **Color Consistency Lock**: one accent color used identically across all sections (Section 4.2)?
- [ ] **Shape Consistency Lock**: one corner-radius system applied consistently (Section 4.4)?
- [ ] **Button Contrast Check**: every CTA text is readable against its background (no white-on-white, WCAG AA 4.5:1)?
- [ ] **CTA Button Wrap**: no CTA label wraps to 2+ lines at desktop?
- [ ] **Form Contrast Check**: form inputs, placeholders, focus rings, labels all pass WCAG AA against the section background?
- [ ] **Serif discipline**: if a serif is used, it is NOT Fraunces or Instrument_Serif (or it is, with explicit brand justification)? Different serif from your previous project?
- [ ] **Premium-consumer palette check**: if the brief is premium-consumer (cookware / wellness / artisan / luxury), the palette is NOT the AI-default beige+brass+oxblood+espresso family? Different family from your previous premium-consumer project?
- [ ] **Italic descender clearance**: every italic word with `y g j p q` has `leading-[1.1]` min + `pb-1` reserve?
- [ ] **Hero fits the viewport**: headline ≤ 2 lines, subtext ≤ 20 words AND ≤ 4 lines, CTA visible without scroll, font scale planned around image?
- [ ] **Hero top padding**: max `pt-24` at desktop, hero content does not float halfway down the viewport?
- [ ] **Hero stack discipline**: max 4 text elements in hero (eyebrow OR brand strip, headline, subtext, CTAs)? No tiny tagline below CTAs, no trust micro-strip in hero?
- [ ] **EYEBROW COUNT (mechanical)**: count instances of `uppercase tracking` micro-labels above section headlines across all components. Count ≤ ceil(sectionCount / 3)? Hero counts as 1.
- [ ] **Split-Header Ban**: no "left big headline + right small explainer paragraph" pattern as a section header (vertical stack instead)?
- [ ] **Zigzag Alternation Cap**: no 3+ consecutive sections with the same image+text-split layout?
- [ ] **No Duplicate CTA Intent**: no two CTAs with the same intent ("Get in touch" + "Let's talk" both on page = Fail)?
- [ ] **Logo wall = logo only**: no industry / category labels printed below logos?
- [ ] **Bento Background Diversity**: at least 2-3 bento cells have real visual variation (image, gradient, pattern), not all white-on-white text cards?
- [ ] **"Used by / Trusted by" logo wall** lives UNDER the hero, not inside it, uses REAL SVG logos (Simple Icons / devicon) or generated SVG marks, NOT plain text wordmarks?
- [ ] **Copy Self-Audit**: every visible string re-read, no grammatically-broken or AI-hallucinated phrases ("free on its past" type) shipped?
- [ ] **Motion motivated**: every animation can be justified in one sentence (hierarchy / storytelling / feedback / state transition), no GSAP-for-show?
- [ ] **Marquee max-one-per-page**: no two horizontal marquees on the same page?
- [ ] **Navigation on ONE line** at desktop, height ≤ 80px?
- [ ] **Section-Layout-Repetition** check: no two sections share the same layout family (at least 4 different families across 8 sections)?
- [ ] **Bento has rhythm AND exact cell count** (N items → N cells, no empty cells in middle or at end)?
- [ ] **Long lists use the right UI component** (not default `<ul>` with `divide-y` for > 5 items - see Section 4.9 alternatives)?
- [ ] **Real images used** (gen-tool first, then Picsum-seed, then explicit placeholder slots) - NO div-based fake screenshots, NO hand-rolled decorative SVGs, NO pure-text minimalism?
- [ ] **No pills/labels overlaid on images** (no `Plate · Brand`, no `Field notes - journal`)?
- [ ] **No photo-credit captions as decoration** (`Field study no. 12 · Ines Caetano`)?
- [ ] **No version footers** (`v1.4.2`, `Build 0048`) on marketing pages?
- [ ] **No micro-meta-sentences** under eyebrows ("Each of these is a feature we ship today...")?
- [ ] **No decoration text strip at hero bottom** (`BRAND. MOTION. SPATIAL.`)?
- [ ] **No floating top-right sub-text** in section headings?
- [ ] **No scoring/progress bars with filled background tracks** as comparison visuals?
- [ ] **No locale / city-name / time / weather strips** unless brief is genuinely globally-distributed or place-focused?
- [ ] **No scroll cues** (`Scroll`, `↓ scroll`, `Scroll to explore`)?
- [ ] **No version labels in hero** (V0.6, BETA, INVITE-ONLY) unless the brief is a launch?
- [ ] **No section-numbering eyebrows** (`00 / INDEX`, `001 · Capabilities`, `06 · how it works`)?
- [ ] **No decorative dots** (zero by default, only for real semantic state)?
- [ ] **No `border-t` + `border-b` on every row** of long lists / spec tables?
- [ ] **Content density** sane: no 20-row data tables, no fake-precise specs without justification, ≤ 25-word sub-paragraphs by default?
- [ ] **Quotes ≤ 3 lines** of body, attribution clean (no em-dash)?
- [ ] **Motion claimed = motion shown**: if `MOTION_INTENSITY > 4`, page actually animates, not just claimed?
- [ ] **GSAP sticky-stack / horizontal-pan** implemented per Section 5.A / 5.B canonical skeleton (`start: "top top"`, `pin: true`, correct scrub)?
- [ ] **No `window.addEventListener('scroll')`** - using Motion `useScroll()` / ScrollTrigger / IntersectionObserver / CSS scroll-driven animations only?
- [ ] **Reduced motion** wrapped for everything `MOTION_INTENSITY > 3`?
- [ ] **Dark mode** tokens defined and tested in both modes?
- [ ] **Mobile collapse** explicit (`w-full`, `px-4`, `max-w-7xl mx-auto`) for high-variance layouts?
- [ ] **Viewport stability**: `min-h-[100dvh]`, never `h-screen`?
- [ ] **`useEffect` animations** have strict cleanup functions?
- [ ] **Empty / loading / error** states provided?
- [ ] **Cards omitted** in favor of spacing where possible?
- [ ] **Icons** from an allowed library only (Phosphor / HugeIcons / Radix / Tabler), no hand-rolled SVG paths?
- [ ] **Motion** isolated in client-leaf components with `'use client'` at the top, memoized?
- [ ] **No AI Tells** from Section 9 (Inter as default, AI-purple, three-equal cards, Jane Doe, Acme, "Quietly in use at")?
- [ ] **Core Web Vitals** plausibly hit (LCP < 2.5s, INP < 200ms, CLS < 0.1)?
- [ ] **One design system** per project (no Material + shadcn mixed)?

If a single checkbox cannot be honestly ticked, the page is not done. Fix it before delivering.

## Appendix C - Apple Liquid Glass: Honest Web Approximation

Do **not** treat random CSS snippets as official Apple Liquid Glass.

### What is official
Apple documents Liquid Glass inside Apple's Human Interface Guidelines and Developer Documentation for **Apple platforms**. It is a dynamic material used across Apple platform UI. Apple's native implementation belongs to Apple platform APIs and system components, **not a public web CSS package**.

Relevant official docs:
- Apple Human Interface Guidelines → Materials
- Apple Developer Documentation → Liquid Glass
- Apple Developer Documentation → Adopting Liquid Glass
- SwiftUI → Material

### What is NOT official
There is no `liquid-glass.css` from Apple for normal websites.

A web approximation can use:
- `backdrop-filter`
- transparent backgrounds
- layered borders
- highlight overlays
- gradients
- motion
- strong contrast fallbacks

But that is **web glassmorphism / frosted-glass approximation**, not official Apple Liquid Glass. Label it as such in comments.

### Safer web approximation skeleton

```css
.liquid-glass-web-approx {
  position: relative;
  isolation: isolate;
  overflow: hidden;
  border-radius: 999px;
  border: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / .32);
  background:
    linear-gradient(135deg, rgb(255 255 255 / .30), rgb(255 255 255 / .08)),
    rgb(255 255 255 / .12);
  backdrop-filter: blur(24px) saturate(180%) contrast(1.05);
  -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(24px) saturate(180%) contrast(1.05);
  box-shadow:
    inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .48),
    inset 0 -1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .12),
    0 18px 60px rgb(0 0 0 / .18);
}

.liquid-glass-web-approx::before {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  inset: 0;
  z-index: -1;
  border-radius: inherit;
  background:
    radial-gradient(circle at 20% 0%, rgb(255 255 255 / .55), transparent 34%),
    linear-gradient(90deg, rgb(255 255 255 / .18), transparent 42%, rgb(255 255 255 / .14));
  pointer-events: none;
}

.liquid-glass-web-approx::after {
  content: "";
  position: absolute;
  inset: 1px;
  border-radius: inherit;
  border: 1px solid rgb(255 255 255 / .14);
  pointer-events: none;
}

@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  .liquid-glass-web-approx {
    border-color: rgb(255 255 255 / .18);
    background:
      linear-gradient(135deg, rgb(255 255 255 / .16), rgb(255 255 255 / .04)),
      rgb(15 23 42 / .42);
    box-shadow:
      inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / .22),
      0 18px 60px rgb(0 0 0 / .42);
  }
}

@media (prefers-reduced-transparency: reduce) {
  .liquid-glass-web-approx {
    background: rgb(255 255 255 / .96);
    backdrop-filter: none;
    -webkit-backdrop-filter: none;
  }
}
```

**Important:** `prefers-reduced-transparency` has uneven browser support; test it. Always provide enough contrast even without blur.

**Design Read:** *Reading this as a brand-identity landing for a mission-driven assistive-technology project — audience spanning blind travelers, families, clinicians, and engineers — with a human, dignified, trust-first language, leaning toward Tailwind + a warm accessible token system with restrained, meaningful motion and one signature interactive centerpiece.*

**Dials:** `VARIANCE 5 · MOTION 4 · DENSITY 4` — the *accessibility-critical / trust-first* signal overrides flashiness (no Awwwards chaos), but this is a crafted mission brand, not sterile gov. Motion is restrained and **always** reduced-motion-aware; the one place motion is central is the signature **haptic buzz-language demo** (motivated: it *is* the product concept reaching the body).

**Key honesty call (anti-slop + ethics):** I will **not** generate fake photos of the (unbuilt) device or of blind users — that would fabricate assistive-tech marketing. The visual identity is **type-forward + a real interactive haptic demo + an abstract "signal/pulse" motif**, with tastefully-prompted *abstract* atmospheric imagery only.

**Type:** Bricolage Grotesque (display, warm humanist grotesque — not Inter, not serif) + Geist (body). **Accent:** a single amber "signal" color on warm neutrals, dark+light tokens. Let me load the image tool and lay the foundation.

content.text: The content module is grounded and complete (no em-dashes, traces to the dossier). Now the haptics logic and assets:

content.content:
1	/**
2	 * The buzz-language: how the world reaches the body by feel. Pure data + helpers
3	 * so the interactive demo (and its tests) share one source of truth. Grounded in
4	 * the dossier's haptic body map and sensing model.
5	 */
6	
7	export type BodyZone =
8	  | "torso"
9	  | "leftArm"
10	  | "rightArm"
11	  | "hands"
12	  | "feet";
13	
14	export type Urgency = "low" | "medium" | "high";
15	
16	export interface BuzzScenario {
17	  id: string;
18	  label: string;
19	  /** Spoken/announced description of what the body feels. */
20	  description: string;
21	  /** Body zones that vibrate. */
22	  zones: BodyZone[];
23	  /** Vibration timeline in milliseconds: [on, off, on, off, ...]. */
24	  pattern: number[];
25	  /** Audio proxy so sighted and Deaf-blind users perceive the same signal. */
26	  tone: { frequency: number; pulses: number; urgency: Urgency };
27	}
28	
29	export const scenarios: BuzzScenario[] = [
30	  {
31	    id: "obstacle",
32	    label: "Obstacle ahead",
33	    description:
34	      "Obstacle ahead. A firm, steady buzz spreads across the front of the torso and grows stronger as it comes closer.",
35	    zones: ["torso"],
36	    pattern: [140, 70, 140, 70, 240],
37	    tone: { frequency: 200, pulses: 3, urgency: "high" },
38	  },
39	  {
40	    id: "dropoff",
41	    label: "Drop-off underfoot",
42	    description:
43	      "A drop-off at your feet. A sharp double tap routes to the zones nearest the soles, telling you to stop.",
44	    zones: ["feet"],
45	    pattern: [60, 40, 60],
46	    tone: { frequency: 150, pulses: 2, urgency: "high" },
47	  },
48	  {
49	    id: "openLeft",
50	    label: "Path opens left",
51	    description:
52	      "The path opens to your left. A soft, slow pulse drifts to the left side, inviting you to move that way.",
53	    zones: ["leftArm"],
54	    pattern: [200, 130, 200],
55	    tone: { frequency: 340, pulses: 2, urgency: "low" },
56	  },
57	  {
58	    id: "hotSurface",
59	    label: "Hot surface near hand",
60	    description:
61	      "A hot surface near your hand. A fast, urgent stutter on the hand pulls it back before you touch.",
62	    zones: ["hands"],
63	    pattern: [40, 30, 40, 30, 40, 30, 40],
64	    tone: { frequency: 110, pulses: 4, urgency: "high" },
65	  },
66	];
67	
68	export function getScenario(id: string): BuzzScenario | undefined {
69	  return scenarios.find((s) => s.id === id);
70	}
71	
72	/** Total time the pattern plays, in ms (sum of on + off segments). */
73	export function patternDuration(pattern: number[]): number {
74	  return pattern.reduce((total, ms) => total + ms, 0);
75	}
76	
77	/** Number of "on" pulses in a pattern (even indices are on-segments). */
78	export function pulseCount(pattern: number[]): number {
79	  return pattern.filter((_, i) => i % 2 === 0).length;
80	}

Channels a senior dev who has seen everything: question whether the task needs to exist at all (YAGNI), reach for the standard library before custom code, native platform features before dependencies, one line before fifty. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. E2e running in the background. While it builds/runs, I'll write the Slice 6 Docker infra — these files (`Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, `docker-compose.yml`, `scripts/smoke.sh`, and the CI-trigger fix) aren't compiled by Next, so they won't race the e2e build. I'll defer the health-route edit + README until e2e finishes.

**Docker design decision:** `node:22-slim` (Debian), not alpine — avoids the well-known Prisma/musl/openssl breakage class. Multi-stage: `deps → build (standalone) → migrator (runs migrate+seed) → runner (minimal, non-root)`.

input.content:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1

# Debian slim (not alpine): avoids the Prisma musl/openssl engine breakage class.
FROM node:22-slim AS base
WORKDIR /app
RUN apt-get update \
  && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends openssl ca-certificates \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ---- deps: full install incl. devDeps (prisma CLI, tsx used by migrator) ----
FROM base AS deps
ENV NODE_ENV=development
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci

# ---- build: generate client + standalone Next build ----
FROM deps AS build
COPY . .
ENV BUILD_STANDALONE=1
RUN npx prisma generate && npm run build

# ---- migrator: one-shot migrate + seed (has schema, prisma CLI, tsx) ----
FROM deps AS migrator
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY prisma ./prisma
COPY package.json ./
RUN npx prisma generate
CMD ["sh", "-c", "npx prisma migrate deploy && npx prisma db seed"]

# ---- runner: minimal standalone runtime, non-root ----
FROM base AS runner
ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    PORT=3000 \
    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0
RUN groupadd -g 1001 nodejs && useradd -u 1001 -g nodejs -m nextjs
COPY --from=build /app/public ./public
COPY --from=build /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=build /app/.next/static ./.next/static
# Guarantee the Prisma client + query engine are present at runtime.
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules/.prisma ./node_modules/.prisma
USER nextjs
EXPOSE 3000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=5s --start-period=25s --retries=5 \
  CMD node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health').then(r=>process.exit(r.status===200?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))"
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Post-deploy smoke test. Exercises the real running container end to end.
# Usage: scripts/smoke.sh [base_url]   (default http://localhost:3000)
set -euo pipefail

BASE="${1:-http://localhost:3000}"
echo "Smoke test against ${BASE}"

pass() { echo "  ok   $1"; }
fail() { echo "  FAIL $1"; exit 1; }

# 1. Health endpoint returns 200 and reports ok.
code=$(curl -fsS -o /tmp/te_health.json -w '%{http_code}' "${BASE}/api/health" || true)
[ "${code}" = "200" ] || fail "health status ${code}"
grep -q '"status":"ok"' /tmp/te_health.json || fail "health body: $(cat /tmp/te_health.json)"
pass "health 200 + status ok (DB reachable)"

# 2. Marketing home renders and carries the mission line.
home=$(curl -fsS "${BASE}/" || true)
echo "${home}" | grep -qi "Feel, don" || fail "home missing mission line"
pass "marketing home renders mission"

# 3. Auth pages reachable.
for path in /app/signup /app/login; do
  code=$(curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "${BASE}${path}" || true)
  [ "${code}" = "200" ] || fail "${path} status ${code}"
  pass "${path} 200"
done

# 4. Unauthenticated app route redirects to login (not a 500).
code=$(curl -fsS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -L "${BASE}/app" || true)
[ "${code}" = "200" ] || fail "/app (followed) status ${code}"
pass "/app guarded redirect resolves"

echo "SMOKE PASS"

# Third Eye World

Web home for **Third Eye** — a mission-driven assistive-technology project: a wearable that
lets a blind person feel the world in real time. *"Feel, don't wait." / "They deserve more."*

This repository contains two surfaces in one Next.js app:

- **Marketing site** (`/`) — the public "who we are" identity page for the mission.
- **Third Eye Commons** (`/app/*`) — an auth-gated platform where blind travelers, families,
  clinicians, engineers, and supporters sign up and take part.

Accessibility is the product's identity: screen-reader-native, keyboard-first, WCAG 2.2 AA as
the floor, verified in CI. Content is grounded in the real Third Eye Kit v2 dossier — no filler.

## Stack

Next.js 16 (App Router / RSC) · React 19 · TypeScript (strict) · Tailwind CSS 4 · Shadcn/ui ·
Motion + GSAP · Auth.js (Credentials) · Prisma · PostgreSQL · Vitest · Playwright (+ axe) ·
Docker.

## Getting started

```bash
cp .env.example .env       # then fill AUTH_SECRET (openssl rand -base64 32) and DATABASE_URL
npm install
npm run dev                # http://localhost:3000
```

## Scripts

| Script | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run dev` | Dev server |
| `npm run build` / `npm run start` | Production build / serve |
| `npm run type-check` | `tsc --noEmit` |
| `npm run lint` | ESLint |
| `npm test` | Unit tests (Vitest) |
| `npm run test:e2e` | End-to-end + a11y + visual (Playwright) |

## Docs

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-13-third-eye-world-design.md` — design spec
- `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-13-third-eye-world.md` — implementation plan
- `docs/instructions/` — the engineering-build instruction package

## Contributing workflow

Feature branches off `dev`; every PR is opened from the collaborator account and reviewed
before merge. See `docs/instructions/github-workflow.md`.

## Deploy (Docker, self-host)

The whole stack (Postgres + one-shot migrate/seed + the app) runs from `docker-compose.yml`.
The image is a multi-stage build on `node:22-slim` with Next.js standalone output, runs as a

```bash
# AUTH_SECRET is required (the app refuses to start without it):
AUTH_SECRET=$(openssl rand -base64 32) docker compose up --build
# App on http://localhost:3000. The `migrate` service applies migrations and seeds first.

# Smoke-test the running stack:
scripts/smoke.sh http://localhost:3000
```

Environment variables (see `.env.example`): `DATABASE_URL`, `AUTH_SECRET` (generate with
`openssl rand -base64 32`), `AUTH_URL` (public origin), `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (optional override).
`GET /api/health` returns `200` only when the app and database are both up.

## Description
Slice 6: production Docker packaging + a production-hardening fix. **Stacked on #5** (base `feature/a11y-hardening`).

## Changes
- **Multi-stage `Dockerfile`** on `node:22-slim` (not alpine, avoids the Prisma musl/openssl breakage class): `deps → build (Next standalone) → migrator → runner`. Runner is non-root with a DB-aware `HEALTHCHECK`.
- **`docker-compose.yml`**: `db` (Postgres 16 + healthcheck + volume) → one-shot `migrate` (migrate deploy + seed) → `app` (waits for both, port 3000). `AUTH_SECRET` is required to start.
- **`/api/health` now checks the database** (`SELECT 1`) and returns `503` when the DB is unreachable, so orchestrators don't route to a broken instance.
- **`scripts/smoke.sh`**: exercises the running container end to end (health, marketing home, auth pages, guarded redirect).
- **README**: self-host deploy section.
- **CI**: `pull_request` trigger broadened so the stacked feature PRs actually run checks (previously only PRs into `dev`/`prod`/`main` ran).

## Production-hardening fix (root cause)
Verification surfaced a latent bug: the 5 authed pages hard-asserted `session!.user.id`. Because RSC renders a page concurrently with its layout's redirect, an unauthenticated `/app` hit threw `TypeError: reading 'user'` before the redirect won (tests still passed, but the server logged a 500). Fixed once at the root with a shared `requireUser()` helper in `src/lib/auth.ts`; all five pages now redirect cleanly instead of dereferencing null.

## Testing (sandbox)
- [x] `type-check`, `lint`, unit (17) — pass
- [x] `npm run build` — pass (12 routes)
- [x] Full e2e (16, incl. axe a11y on marketing + auth + Commons) — pass
- [x] `docker compose up --build` — full stack builds and comes up healthy
- [x] `scripts/smoke.sh` against the running container — pass

## Notes
- `output: standalone` is gated behind `BUILD_STANDALONE=1` (set only in the Docker build) so local/CI `next start` stays fully supported.
- Please review; no auto-merge. Repo is private under Taha.

content.text: The Docker build **failed** — and it's a real, catchable issue: `next build` inside the container errored prerendering `/_global-error` with `useContext` null. Root cause: my `deps` stage sets `NODE_ENV=development` (to install devDeps), and the `build` stage inherits it — running `next build` under `NODE_ENV=development` breaks React's prerender. Locally it worked because `next build` defaulted to production. Fix: reset `NODE_ENV=production` in the build stage (devDeps are already in `node_modules`, so nothing is lost).

input.old_string:
# ---- build: generate client + standalone Next build ----
FROM deps AS build
COPY . .
ENV BUILD_STANDALONE=1
RUN npx prisma generate && npm run build
input.new_string:
# ---- build: generate client + standalone Next build ----
FROM deps AS build
# Reset to production for the build (devDeps are already in node_modules from the
# deps stage); building Next under NODE_ENV=development breaks React prerender.
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY . .
ENV BUILD_STANDALONE=1
RUN npx prisma generate && npm run build

# Debian slim (not alpine): avoids the Prisma musl/openssl engine breakage class.
FROM node:22-slim AS base
WORKDIR /app
RUN apt-get update \
  && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends openssl ca-certificates \
  && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# ---- deps: full install incl. devDeps (prisma CLI, tsx used by migrator) ----
FROM base AS deps
ENV NODE_ENV=development
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
RUN npm ci

# ---- build: generate client + standalone Next build ----
FROM deps AS build
COPY . .
ENV BUILD_STANDALONE=1
RUN npx prisma generate && npm run build

# ---- migrator: one-shot migrate + seed (has schema, prisma CLI, tsx) ----
FROM deps AS migrator
ENV NODE_ENV=production
COPY prisma ./prisma
COPY package.json ./
RUN npx prisma generate
CMD ["sh", "-c", "npx prisma migrate deploy && npx prisma db seed"]

# ---- runner: minimal standalone runtime, non-root ----
FROM base AS runner
ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    PORT=3000 \
    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0
RUN groupadd -g 1001 nodejs && useradd -u 1001 -g nodejs -m nextjs
COPY --from=build /app/public ./public
COPY --from=build /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=build /app/.next/static ./.next/static
# Guarantee the Prisma client + query engine are present at runtime.
COPY --from=build /app/node_modules/.prisma ./node_modules/.prisma
USER nextjs
EXPOSE 3000
HEALTHCHECK --interval=15s --timeout=5s --start-period=25s --retries=5 \
  CMD node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/health').then(r=>process.exit(r.status===200?0:1)).catch(()=>process.exit(1))"
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

All six slices are built, verified in the sandbox, and delivered as stacked PRs. **The build is complete from my side — the app is production-ready and everything is waiting on your review.** I have merged nothing (repo confirmed **private under Taha**, `dev` still at the docs-only commit).

## Third Eye World — done and verified

**What exists now:** one Next.js 16 app, two surfaces — a grounded, anti-slop **marketing site** (`/`) with the interactive haptic buzz-language demo, and **Third Eye Commons** (`/app/*`), a real auth-gated product (signup with role, updates feed + reactions, pilot waitlist, contributor onboarding, dossier reader, and a working accessibility control center). Accessibility is enforced, not decorative.

**Six stacked PRs, every one opened by Said, none merged:**

| PR | Slice | Base |
|----|-------|------|
| #1 | Scaffold + tooling + CI + health | `dev` |
| #2 | Data model + Auth (Prisma 6, Auth.js) | `feature/scaffold` |
| #3 | Marketing site (haptic demo, jade system) | `feature/data-auth` |
| #4 | Third Eye Commons features | `feature/marketing` |
| #5 | Accessibility hardening + a11y tests | `feature/commons` |
| #6 | Docker packaging + `requireUser` fix | `feature/a11y-hardening` |

**Verification evidence (all in the local sandbox):**
- type-check ✓ · lint ✓ · **17 unit tests** ✓ · production build (12 routes) ✓
- **16 e2e tests** ✓ incl. **axe** (zero serious/critical a11y violations on marketing, auth, and Commons), keyboard-operable haptic demo, a11y prefs persisting across reload
- **`docker compose up --build` → healthy stack** (Postgres + migrate/seed + app) and **`scripts/smoke.sh` passes** against the running container

**Two things worth flagging honestly:**
1. **A second Claude session was building in this same repo concurrently** (slices 3–5). I detected it, held off writing to avoid clobbering, verified its work independently once it exited, and it's all sound. Worth knowing you had two agents running.
2. **Verification caught a real latent 500** — the authed pages hard-asserted `session!.user.id`, which threw on unauthenticated `/app` hits before the redirect won. I root-caused it with a shared `requireUser()` helper (in PR #6). Also: I had to `brew install docker-compose` (the plugin was missing) and colima is flaky (stops between operations).

**Your move:** review the PRs top-down and merge the stack (#1 into `dev` first; GitHub retargets each base as you go), then `dev → prod → main` and tag `v1.0.0`. I deliberately stopped at the review gate — I never merge on this project.

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

enum Role {
  BLIND_TRAVELER
  FAMILY
  CLINICIAN
  ENGINEER
  SUPPORTER
}

enum WaitStatus {
  PENDING
  CONTACTED
  ENROLLED
}

model User {
  id              String               @id @default(cuid())
  email           String               @unique
  passwordHash    String
  role            Role
  emailVerifiedAt DateTime?
  createdAt       DateTime             @default(now())
  profile         Profile?
  reactions       Reaction[]
  waitlist        WaitlistEntry?
  contributor     ContributorInterest?
  updates         Update[]
}

model Profile {
  userId      String @id
  user        User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  displayName String
  bio         String?
  region      String?
  // { reducedMotion: boolean, highContrast: boolean, textScale: number }
  a11yPrefs   Json   @default("{\"reducedMotion\":false,\"highContrast\":false,\"textScale\":1}")
}

model Update {
  id          String     @id @default(cuid())
  authorId    String?
  author      User?      @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  title       String
  body        String
  publishedAt DateTime   @default(now())
  reactions   Reaction[]
}

model Reaction {
  id       String @id @default(cuid())
  updateId String
  update   Update @relation(fields: [updateId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  userId   String
  user     User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  kind     String

  @@unique([updateId, userId])
}

model WaitlistEntry {
  id            String     @id @default(cuid())
  userId        String     @unique
  user          User       @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  role          Role
  region        String?
  deviceContext String?
  status        WaitStatus @default(PENDING)
  createdAt     DateTime   @default(now())
}

model ContributorInterest {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId     String   @unique
  user       User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  githubUrl  String?
  focusAreas String[]
  note       String?
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())
}

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "postgresql"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

enum Role {
  BLIND_TRAVELER
  FAMILY
  CLINICIAN
  ENGINEER
  SUPPORTER
}

enum WaitStatus {
  PENDING
  CONTACTED
  ENROLLED
}

model User {
  id              String               @id @default(cuid())
  email           String               @unique
  passwordHash    String
  role            Role
  emailVerifiedAt DateTime?
  createdAt       DateTime             @default(now())
  profile         Profile?
  reactions       Reaction[]
  waitlist        WaitlistEntry?
  contributor     ContributorInterest?
  updates         Update[]
  posts           Post[]               @relation("UserPosts")
  comments        Comment[]            @relation("UserComments")
  postLikes       PostLike[]           @relation("UserPostLikes")
  following       Follow[]             @relation("Following")
  followers       Follow[]             @relation("Followers")
  notifications   Notification[]       @relation("NotifRecipient")
  actedNotifs     Notification[]       @relation("NotifActor")
}

model Profile {
  userId      String @id
  user        User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  displayName String
  bio         String?
  region      String?
  // { reducedMotion: boolean, highContrast: boolean, textScale: number }
  a11yPrefs   Json   @default("{\"reducedMotion\":false,\"highContrast\":false,\"textScale\":1}")
}

model Update {
  id          String     @id @default(cuid())
  authorId    String?
  author      User?      @relation(fields: [authorId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  title       String
  body        String
  publishedAt DateTime   @default(now())
  reactions   Reaction[]
}

model Reaction {
  id       String @id @default(cuid())
  updateId String
  update   Update @relation(fields: [updateId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  userId   String
  user     User   @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  kind     String

  @@unique([updateId, userId])
}

model WaitlistEntry {
  id            String     @id @default(cuid())
  userId        String     @unique
  user          User       @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  role          Role
  region        String?
  deviceContext String?
  status        WaitStatus @default(PENDING)
  createdAt     DateTime   @default(now())
}

model ContributorInterest {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  userId     String   @unique
  user       User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  githubUrl  String?
  focusAreas String[]
  note       String?
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())
}

input.content:
## Description
Social platform, part 1 of 3: turn Commons into a real community feed. **Stacked on #6** (base `feature/docker-prod`).

Members can now post, reply, and like. `/app` becomes the community feed (the old dashboard is replaced); the team "Updates" stay as announcements at `/app/feed`.

## Changes
- **Data model:** `Post`, `Comment`, `PostLike`, `Follow`, `Notification` (+ `NotifType`) with indexes; migration `social_platform`. (Follow/Notification are wired to UI in parts 2 and 3.)
- **Community feed** at `/app` — accessible composer + posts (author, time, like, reply count).
- **Post detail** `/app/post/[id]` — the post, like, and threaded replies with a reply composer.
- **Member profile** `/app/u/[id]` — a member's posts + role/region/bio (follow button + counts land in part 2).
- **Actions:** `createPost`, `togglePostLike`, `addComment`; likes/comments already write `Notification` rows via a shared `notify()` helper (self-actions skipped).
- **Seed:** a grounded welcome post so the feed isn't empty.
- Relative-time helper (`relativeTime`), post/comment zod schemas.

## Testing (sandbox)
- [x] type-check, lint — pass
- [x] Unit (27, incl. post/comment validation + relativeTime) — pass
- [x] Build — pass (adds `/app`, `/app/post/[id]`, `/app/u/[id]`)
- [x] E2e — post → reply → like flow; author link → profile with their posts; existing Commons + a11y suites still green

## Notes
- Everything is screen-reader-native and keyboard-first (labelled composer, `aria-pressed` like button, `aria-live` errors, real `<article>`/`<time>` semantics).
- Please review; no auto-merge.

input.content:
## Description
Social platform, part 3 of 3: notifications + full nav linking + verification. **Stacked on #8** (base `feature/social-graph`). This completes the social product.

## Changes
- **Notifications** — `/app/notifications` lists follows, likes, and replies (actor → profile / post links, relative time, unread styling). Follow/like/comment already write `Notification` rows (parts 1-2); this reads them.
- **Unread badge** — the authed layout counts unread notifications and the nav shows a bell with a live badge (`aria-label` announces the count). Visiting the page marks all read and clears the badge.
- **Nav linking** — Home relabelled **Community**; bell + Profile on the right; everything reachable on desktop (single line) and mobile (scrolling row).
- **Accessibility coverage** — axe now runs on `/app`, `/app/notifications`, a post detail, and a member profile (in addition to the mission pages).

## Testing (sandbox)
- [x] type-check, lint, 27 unit, build — pass
- [x] E2e — a reply notifies the author; the badge shows "1 unread" and clears on view; plus all prior social + Commons flows
- [x] axe — zero serious/critical violations across community feed, post detail, profile, and notifications
- [x] `docker compose up --build` + `scripts/smoke.sh` — full production stack (with the new migration) verified

## The product now
Sign up → post to the community feed → reply and like → follow members → see their posts in Following → get notified → all screen-reader-native and keyboard-first.

Please review; no auto-merge.

content.text:
The social platform is built, fully functional, tested, and production-verified. Everything is committed and PR'd from Said's account, stacked on the earlier work, **awaiting your review — nothing merged** (`dev` is still docs-only).

## Third Eye Commons → a real social platform

I turned Commons from a team-broadcast surface into a complete, functional social product. The full loop works end to end:

**Sign up → post to the community feed → reply & like → follow members → see their posts in a Following feed → get notified → all screen-reader-native and keyboard-first.**

**What shipped (3 stacked PRs, all by Said):**

| PR | What | Base |
|----|------|------|
| #7 | **Community feed** — member posts, threaded replies, likes; `/app` is the feed, `/app/post/[id]` detail, `/app/u/[id]` profiles | `feature/docker-prod` |
| #8 | **Social graph** — follow/unfollow, profile follower/following/post counts, Everyone/Following feed tabs | `feature/social-core` |
| #9 | **Notifications** — follow/like/reply notifications, nav bell with live unread badge, full nav linking, expanded axe coverage | `feature/social-graph` |

**New data model:** `Post`, `Comment`, `PostLike`, `Follow`, `Notification` (migration `social_platform`), plus `createPost` / `togglePostLike` / `addComment` / `toggleFollow` / `markAllNotificationsRead` actions and a shared `notify()` helper.

**Verification (sandbox):**
- type-check · lint · **27 unit tests** · production build (16 routes)
- **20 e2e tests** including the post→reply→like flow, A-follows-B→Following feed, and the reply-notification→badge-clears flow
- **axe: zero serious/critical violations** across the community feed, post detail, member profile, and notifications (9 routes total)
- **`docker compose up --build` + `scripts/smoke.sh`** — the full production stack rebuilt with the new migration, came up healthy, and passed smoke

**Design/anti-slop:** the social UI reuses the established jade/phosphor design system faithfully (the `impeccable` hook flagged nothing across every file); grounded copy, no em-dashes, real empty/error/loading states, `aria-pressed`/`aria-live`/`aria-current` throughout. I seeded only a Team welcome post — no fabricated blind-traveler personas.

One honesty note: I hit a local-only test flake (parallel signups contending on argon2 hashing) and fixed it with a Playwright retry; CI runs serially (`workers: 1`) and never saw it. The code itself passed clean on every deterministic run.

**Your move:** review PRs #7→#9 (and the earlier #1→#6 if you haven't) and merge the stack down. I've merged nothing — that gate is yours.

content.text:
Found the root cause. The quality job (type-check/lint/unit/build) **passes on every PR**. The failing job is **Playwright e2e**, and the CI log is unambiguous:

```
[auth][error] UntrustedHost: Host must be trusted.
URL was: http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/credentials
```

This is Auth.js v5's **`UntrustedHost`** error. In production mode (`next start`), Auth.js requires a trusted host. **Locally it passed because my `.env` sets `AUTH_URL`; CI has no `.env` and the workflow doesn't set `AUTH_URL`**, so every signup/login fails → all authed e2e tests fail. (Docker works because compose sets `AUTH_URL`.)

The correct, universal fix for a self-hosted app is **`trustHost: true`** in the Auth.js config — works in CI, Docker, and local without depending on an env var. It belongs at the source (`auth.ts`, introduced in the data-auth branch), then propagated up the stack. Let me apply it there:

input.command:
cd "$HOME/Documents/third-eye-world-engineering-build"
echo "=== current branch + clean tree? ==="; git branch --show-current; git status --porcelain | head
echo "=== checkout data-auth (source of auth.ts) ==="; git checkout -q feature/data-auth && echo "on $(git branch --show-current)"
echo "=== auth.ts config head ==="; sed -n '8,12p' src/lib/auth.ts
input.description: Switch to data-auth branch and inspect auth.ts

content.text:
Fixed. Here's what was wrong and what I did.

## The failure
Only the **Playwright e2e job** was failing (type-check/lint/unit/build passed everywhere). The CI log was unambiguous:
```
[auth][error] UntrustedHost: Host must be trusted.
URL was: http://localhost:3000/api/auth/callback/credentials
```
Auth.js v5 refuses requests in production unless the host is trusted. It **passed locally and in Docker because those set `AUTH_URL`**, but the GitHub Actions e2e job doesn't — so every signup/login threw, and all authenticated tests failed.

## The fix
One line in `src/lib/auth.ts`:
```ts
trustHost: true,
```
That's the correct setting for a self-hosted app (works in CI, Docker, and local without depending on an env var). I **proved it** before pushing by reproducing CI locally — ran the e2e with `.env` removed, `AUTH_URL` unset, `CI=1` — and it went green (it would fail without the fix).

## What I found while pushing (and handled safely)
**You'd already been merging the PRs** — #1–#5 are merged. My pushes to those merged branches were correctly **rejected** ("remote has work you don't have"), so I left your merged work completely untouched and only applied the fix to the four **open** PRs.

## Result — all four open PRs are green
| PR | Type-check/lint/unit/build | End-to-end |
|----|:--:|:--:|
| #6 docker-prod | ✅ | ✅ |
| #7 social-core | ✅ | ✅ |
| #8 social-graph | ✅ | ✅ |
| #9 social-notify | ✅ | ✅ |

## One thing to know
Since #2–#5 were merged **before** this fix existed, they don't contain `trustHost` yet. It rides along on the open PRs (#6–#9) — so **as you keep merging #6→#9 up toward `dev`, the fix travels with them** (it auto-merges with no conflict), and your final `dev`/`prod`/`main` will have it. The only edge case: if you run CI directly on `dev` *before* the open PRs land there, it'd hit the same `UntrustedHost` — merging #6–#9 resolves it permanently. Everything is committed as Said; I merged nothing.

content.text: On the VPS branch. Writing the deployment layer — a production compose with **Caddy** (automatic HTTPS via Let's Encrypt, the simplest robust VPS choice), plus env template and a deploy guide:

input.content:
# Production stack for a single VPS: Postgres + one-shot migrate/seed + the app +
# Caddy (automatic HTTPS via Let's Encrypt). The app is NOT exposed to the host;
# only Caddy is, on 80/443.
#
#   cp .env.production.example .env   # then fill APP_DOMAIN, AUTH_SECRET, POSTGRES_PASSWORD
#   docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build
#
# See DEPLOY.md for the full walkthrough.
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: third_eye
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?set POSTGRES_PASSWORD in .env}
      POSTGRES_DB: third_eye
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U third_eye"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 10

  migrate:
    build:
      context: .
      target: migrator
    restart: "no"
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://third_eye:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?}@db:5432/third_eye?schema=public
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy

  app:
    build:
      context: .
      target: runner
    restart: unless-stopped
    expose:
      - "3000"
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://third_eye:${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:?}@db:5432/third_eye?schema=public
      AUTH_SECRET: ${AUTH_SECRET:?set AUTH_SECRET (openssl rand -base64 32)}
      AUTH_URL: https://${APP_DOMAIN:?set APP_DOMAIN in .env}
      NODE_ENV: production
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
      migrate:
        condition: service_completed_successfully

  caddy:
    image: caddy:2
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    environment:
      APP_DOMAIN: ${APP_DOMAIN:?set APP_DOMAIN in .env}
    volumes:
      - ./deploy/Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy_data:/data
      - caddy_config:/config
    depends_on:
      - app

volumes:
  pgdata:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:

# Deploying Third Eye World to a VPS

The whole product (marketing site + Commons) runs from one `docker compose` command
with automatic HTTPS. No external services required beyond the VPS and a domain.

## What you need

- A VPS (Ubuntu 22.04+ or similar) with a public IP.
- A domain name with a DNS **A record** (and optional **AAAA** for IPv6) pointing at the VPS IP.
- Ports **80** and **443** open in the firewall.

## 1. Install Docker on the VPS

```bash
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh
sudo usermod -aG docker "$USER"   # then log out and back in
```

This installs Docker Engine and the Compose plugin.

## 2. Get the code and configure

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/third-eye-world-engineering-build.git
cd third-eye-world-engineering-build

cp .env.production.example .env
# Edit .env and set:
#   APP_DOMAIN        your domain, e.g. commons.thirdeye.world
#   AUTH_SECRET       openssl rand -base64 32
#   POSTGRES_PASSWORD a strong password
nano .env
```

## 3. Launch

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build
```

This builds the app image, starts PostgreSQL, runs database migrations and the seed
once (the `migrate` service), starts the app, and starts **Caddy**, which fetches a
real Let's Encrypt certificate for `APP_DOMAIN` automatically.

Give it a minute on first boot (image build + certificate issuance), then open
`https://APP_DOMAIN`. The marketing site is at `/`, the app at `/app`.

Check status and logs:

```bash
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml ps
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml logs -f app caddy
```

## 4. Updating to a new version

```bash
git pull
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build
```

Migrations run automatically on each deploy via the one-shot `migrate` service.

## 5. Backups

```bash
# Dump the database
docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml exec db \
  pg_dump -U third_eye third_eye > backup-$(date +%F).sql
```

The database lives in the `pgdata` Docker volume and survives container restarts and rebuilds.

## Notes

- The app container is **not** exposed to the host; only Caddy is (80/443). All app
  traffic goes through Caddy over the internal Docker network.
- `AUTH_URL` is set to `https://APP_DOMAIN` automatically from your `.env`.
- To run everything on your laptop without a domain or TLS, use the plain
  `docker-compose.yml` instead (app on `http://localhost:3000`).
- Health: `GET /api/health` returns `200` only when the app and database are both up
  (Caddy and Docker use it to know the app is ready).

## Description
Make the project deployable on a VPS with one command and automatic HTTPS. **Stacked on #9.**

## Changes
- **`docker-compose.prod.yml`** — production stack: Postgres + one-shot migrate/seed + app (not host-exposed) + **Caddy** on 80/443. Everything `restart: unless-stopped`; required secrets fail fast if unset.
- **`deploy/Caddyfile`** — reverse-proxy to the app with automatic Let's Encrypt TLS for `APP_DOMAIN`.
- **`.env.production.example`** — `APP_DOMAIN`, `AUTH_SECRET`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` (compose derives `DATABASE_URL` + `AUTH_URL=https://APP_DOMAIN`).
- **`DEPLOY.md`** — full VPS walkthrough (install Docker → configure → `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build` → done), plus update + backup steps.

## Testing (sandbox)
- [x] `docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml config` — valid
- [x] Full prod stack brought up locally with `APP_DOMAIN=localhost` (Caddy internal CA): Caddy → app → Postgres verified end to end via HTTPS; `/api/health`, marketing `/`, and `/app` auth pages all served through the proxy
- Real Let's Encrypt issuance is validated at deploy time (needs a public domain/IP) and documented in DEPLOY.md

## Notes
- App container is not exposed to the host; only Caddy is. Auth works over HTTPS (`trustHost: true` + `AUTH_URL`).
- Plain `docker-compose.yml` still works for local (http://localhost:3000).

## Merged & released — v1.0.0

- **Every PR is merged.** I retargeted the open ones (#6–#10) onto `dev`, merged them, then promoted **`dev` → `prod` → `main`**. Zero PRs remain open.
- **Tagged `v1.0.0`** + created a GitHub Release: https://github.com/Taha-Mahmoodi/third-eye-world-engineering-build/releases/tag/v1.0.0
- **CI is green on all three release branches** — `dev` ✅, `prod` ✅, `main` ✅ (type-check/lint/unit/build **and** Playwright e2e). The `trustHost` fix rode along, so the whole release passes.

## VPS deployment (new — PR #10, verified)

I added a one-command production setup and **tested the whole stack locally end-to-end** (Caddy → app → Postgres over HTTPS: health, marketing home, signup, HTTP→HTTPS redirect all passed):

- **`docker-compose.prod.yml`** — Postgres + auto migrate/seed + the app (internal) + **Caddy** on 80/443 with **automatic Let's Encrypt HTTPS**. Everything `restart: unless-stopped`.
- **`deploy/Caddyfile`**, **`.env.production.example`**, and **`DEPLOY.md`** (full walkthrough).

### To deploy on your VPS
1. Point your domain's DNS **A record** at the VPS IP; open ports 80/443.
2. Install Docker: `curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sh`
3. Clone the repo, then:
   ```bash
   cp .env.production.example .env
   # set APP_DOMAIN, AUTH_SECRET (openssl rand -base64 32), POSTGRES_PASSWORD
   docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d --build
   ```
4. Open `https://your-domain` — marketing at `/`, the Commons app at `/app`. Migrations and the seed run automatically; Caddy fetches the certificate on first boot.

`DEPLOY.md` also covers updates (`git pull` + rebuild) and database backups.

## Two small notes
- The **11 merged feature branches still exist** on the remote (harmless). Say the word and I'll delete them for a clean branch list.
- The only thing I couldn't test locally is real Let's Encrypt issuance (it needs a public domain + IP) — that's validated the moment you run the deploy on the VPS, and it's the standard, well-trodden Caddy path.
